claims.text: Adding approximately 3 at% Si and applying solution treatment and annealing will promote Si segregation to grain boundaries in HfZrTiTa0.53.
Si segregation will enhance grain-boundary cohesion.
The intervention will increase uniform tensile elongation to approximately 20%.
An increase from 13.5% elongation to approximately 20% constitutes a greater-than-50% improvement.
The intervention will preserve a yield strength of approximately 786 MPa.
The intervention will preserve a compressive strength of approximately 1314 MPa.
The intervention will preserve impact-triggered energy release.
Cast HfZrTiTa0.53 has a baseline uniform tensile elongation of approximately 13.5%.
Solution treatment at about 1200°C followed by annealing at about 800°C will permit Si segregation to grain boundaries.
Si-enriched interfacial films may form at grain boundaries.
Enhanced grain-boundary cohesion will reduce susceptibility to intergranular cracking under tensile stress.
Segregated Si lowers grain-boundary energy in the modified alloy.
Lower grain-boundary energy mitigates embrittlement and impedes intergranular crack initiation and propagation.
The ductility prediction applies at room temperature under tensile loading near a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has previously demonstrated high impact-triggered energy release.
Prior evidence supports grain-boundary segregation as an effective means of improving ductility.

contradictions.description: The stated values of 13.5% and 20% imply an improvement of about 48.1%, not greater than 50%.
Both fields characterize the reported 13.5% terminal strain as uniform tensile elongation, although the task context does not establish that the reported terminal strain came from a tensile test.
